lines.text: An Android app with no code can trap a phone in a crash loop.
lines.note: and it never has to open

lines.text: An Android app is really a ZIP file. Each file inside says how it is stored and how big it is.
lines.title: What an APK is

lines.text: One part of Android skips the size check for odd storage types. Another part trusts that size.
lines.title: Two readers disagree

lines.text: Reading the empty space kills the process. If it is a core service, the phone restarts and fails again.
lines.title: The crash loop

lines.text: Researchers reproduced it on Android seventeen. It affects Android ten and above.
lines.title: How far it reaches

lines.text: Google said it is outside the scope of a security fix. Restarting and safe mode do not help.
lines.title: No quick fix

lines.text: Two parts of a system must read the same file the same way. Mismatches become security bugs.
lines.title: Takeaways
